ownership_label_interleave_audit.purpose: explain why the proximity ownership boundary is FRAGMENTED (25 components) instead of a coherent 1-D contour
ownership_label_interleave_audit.interpretation: Every seam endpoint is a MIXED-label vertex: its 1-ring contains both THUMB-labelled and INDEX-labelled neighbours (typically 2 + 2).  Not one vertex is an isolated label island.  The THUMB/INDEX label field inside the RSSF contact zone is therefore a fine-grained INTERLEAVED MIXTURE over a surface that is geodesically a single digit.  That is the exact signature of a nearest-chain proximity test whose two candidate distances are nearly equal across the whole zone: the winner flips at random, so the resulting 'boundary' is 25 disconnected fragments (degree histogram {1:54, 2:34, 3:4}) rather than one contour.

mesh_true_geodesic_ownership.interpretation: the mesh-true THUMB|INDEX boundary only ever occurs at the thumb base (arc 42.7-58.7 mm, the anatomical first web).  The proximity heuristic adds 61 boundary edges along the thumb distal phalanx (arc 75.5-93.9 mm) where no true boundary exists, and no edge of the 67 is a genuine cross-digit edge.
